rubrics.criterion: The internal size-recording pair on the shared base element — the cached host-size field and the method that compares against the cache and force-re-renders the host — is removed so that neither member survives anywhere in the production sources.
rubrics.rationale: This pair is the anchor of the dead island in this instance: it is the shared-tier residue the other components' leftovers route through, and leaving any part of it behind keeps the smallest possible repair incomplete.

rubrics.criterion: Both non-exported module-level geometry functions in the shared drawing-helper module — the panel-inset computation and the scale-factor computation that call each other — are removed; neither function remains at module scope.
rubrics.rationale: They form the mutually referencing module pair that textual reference counting and the compiler's unused checks both misjudge; removing them is a distinct decision from removing class members and proves the solver handled module-scope leftovers.

rubrics.criterion: The slider's leftover manual thumb-recentering path is removed in full: the recentering method, the private pivot computation it calls, and the nominal knob-radius field that computation reads all disappear from the component.
rubrics.rationale: This site is the canonical in-class dead chain (protected entry to private helper to protected field); a solver who deletes only the outer method or only the field leaves an incoherent half-repair.

rubrics.criterion: In both slot-driven selection components — the combo dropdown and the listbox — the leftover index-driven programmatic selection entries are removed, together with the private notification helpers that re-fire the retired 'select' event name.
rubrics.rationale: The same leftover pattern exists on both sides of the selection family; the instance requires recognizing it as a family-wide residue and removing it consistently in both components rather than in one.

rubrics.criterion: The unused label-span formatting helper of the progress component and the unused frame-interval pacing helper of the spinner component are both removed.
rubrics.rationale: These are the single-component zero-caller residues; removing them shows the sweep covered the per-component tiers as well as the shared tiers.

rubrics.criterion: The removal is complete on both the integrated tiers named in the prompt and everywhere else the same unreachability relation holds in the production sources: no internal member or non-exported module function remains that is reachable only from other unreachable helpers.
rubrics.rationale: The selected prompt asks for a library-wide sweep; this checks the solver applied the responsibility rule generally instead of stopping at the explicitly named areas.

rubrics.criterion: The cross-file and cross-member couplings of the removed helpers are handled as removals too: the component-side helpers that routed through the base element's recording hook disappear together with that hook (no remaining code in any module references a deleted member), and the module-scope geometry pair is deleted as a unit with neither function left calling the other.
rubrics.rationale: Coordination is the point of this instance: the injected residue spans files, so a repair confined to one file at a time either breaks compilation or strands live-looking references.

rubrics.criterion: The patch does not delete or alter the live counterparts of the removed leftovers: the keyboard-driven selection chains (the live stepping that picks the adjacent item), the item-click selection flow, the slot refresh and value/aria update, and the live event dispatchers of both selection components remain intact and still reachable.
rubrics.rationale: Per-instance over-pruning risk: the dead index-selection entries sit directly beside live look-alike members with nearly identical bodies; this distinguishes a correct cleanup from a regex-style deletion of everything selection-related.

rubrics.criterion: The patch leaves no orphaned residue of the removed material: no leftover state field, constant, import, or comment line that existed only to serve the deleted helpers, no emptied-out method bodies kept in place of removal, and no synthetic self-references or no-op call sites added so a leftover would look used.
rubrics.rationale: This instance's leftovers were introduced with their own comments and supporting fields; a complete resolution removes that whole introduced cohort rather than only the method declarations.

rubrics.criterion: The leftovers are not made unreachable by relocation or disguise — e.g. moving them into demo pages or build-excluded files, renaming them onto live names, or wiring them into live flows as no-op placeholders — instead of being removed from the library.
rubrics.rationale: Grades the semantic intent of the cleanup: hiding the members where the production reachability analysis cannot see them satisfies the letter of 'unused' but defeats the maintenance goal the task states.

rubrics.criterion: The public API and the event contract are unchanged: exported classes and types, custom element names and registrations, their attributes and properties and CSS custom properties, static styles, and the events fired by live flows — including the slider's value-change event and the selection components' item-selected notifications — still fire with the same names and payloads, and the retired 'select' event name is not (re)introduced as a live notification.
rubrics.rationale: The removed private dispatchers re-fire a retired event name right next to the live one; this item pins the boundary that a repair must not disturb the real notification paths while removing the dead ones.

rubrics.criterion: Live internal behavior is preserved: keyboard navigation and programmatic stepping through slot items in both selection components, the drop-panel show/hide cycle with its aria attributes, the spinner's requestAnimationFrame loop, duration handling and cursor movement, and the progress percentage label plus hachure fill computation behave exactly as before the cleanup (no modifications to those live methods beyond the removal of their dead siblings).
rubrics.rationale: The dead leftovers duplicate the vocabulary of these live flows (duration math, label math, pivot math); this item catches collateral edits to the live twins during deletion, which the instance's proximity of dead and live code makes the most plausible regression.
